```{r setup, message=F, warning=F, echo=F}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = F, warning = F, echo = F)
theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 12))
source("helper_functions/ndar_qc.R")      # read_ndar
source("helper_functions/wg_scores.R")

cached <- new.env(); load("data/nda_private/cached_data.Rds", envir = cached)  # from 01
cached <- as.list(cached)
raw    <- read_ndar("data/ASD CDI data/mci_words_gestures01.txt")$data
load("data/eng_wg_raw_data.Rds")          # eng_wg (Wordbank, 8–18 months)
priors <- read_csv("in_files/collection_asd_priors.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

nd <- ndar_wg_scores(cached, raw); wbl <- wordbank_wg_scores(eng_wg)
nd_s <- add_derived(nd$scores); wb_s <- add_derived(wbl$scores)
norms <- fit_norms(wb_s)
nd_z <- apply_norms(nd_s, norms); wb_z <- apply_norms(wb_s, norms)
zs <- paste0("z_", names(SCORES)); names(zs) <- names(SCORES)
B <- 1000; set.seed(2026)
```

`07` found that the word-by-word vocabulary profile separates NDAR children from Wordbank
children but does not track autism, while overall vocabulary level for age does. Level,
though, measures delay rather than autism. This notebook tests two Words & Gestures (WG)
measures that are more specific to autism, using the same label-free checks:

- **Gestures**, especially the 12 *First Communicative Gestures* (show, give, point, wave,
  reach to be picked up, ...). Reduced pointing and showing are among the better-replicated
  early signs of autism.
- **The comprehension–production gap**, words understood given words said. In the
  late-talk work it was the strongest single predictor. In autism, comprehension is often
  as delayed as production, so the gap is expected to be *smaller*.

Every score is normed on Wordbank English WG (`r nrow(wb_z)` children, 8–18 months) and
oriented so that **low = the direction expected for autism**. The orientation was fixed
before looking at NDAR.

| Score | Definition |
|---|---|
| Words produced, words understood | Percentile for age among Wordbank children of the same month, as a z-score |
| First communicative gestures (FCG), early gestures (FCG + games and routines), later gestures (actions, pretend play, imitation) | Same |
| Comprehension given production (the gap) | Standardized residual of comprehension from a Wordbank regression on age and production (empirical-logit scale, splines) |
| FCG given words and later gestures | Residual of FCG given age, production, comprehension and later gestures |
| Later gestures given words | Residual of later gestures given age, production and comprehension |

The two FCG and later-gesture residual scores ask whether a child gestures less than
children with the *same* vocabulary. If so, the signal is beyond delay.

## 1. Data

### A coding fix for WG comprehension

Building these scores exposed a coding error in `01`. In datasets 14747 and 16640
(collections 19 and 2027), the lab's stored "words understood" total equals the number
of items coded 0 or 1 for **every** child. So these datasets use 0 = understands only,
1 = says, 2 or blank = neither. `01` had read code 2 as "understands only". That made
most of their children's comprehension equal to their production, and gave the rest
implausibly large comprehension. `infer_wg_coding()` now also picks the comprehension
scheme that reproduces the stored total. Production, and every result from `03`–`07`,
is unchanged: the rerun leaves `admins`, `d_asd_ws` and the WG `value` column identical.

```{r coding}
cached$wg_coding %>%
  left_join(distinct(cached$admins %>% filter(form == "WG"), dataset_id, collection_id),
            by = "dataset_id") %>%
  semi_join(nd_s %>% distinct(collection_id), by = "collection_id") %>%
  filter(dataset_id %in% (cached$admins %>% filter(form == "WG", one_per_child,
                                                    item_profile_ok) %>% pull(dataset_id))) %>%
  transmute(Collection = collection_id, Dataset = dataset_id,
            `"Says" code` = produce_code, `Understood =` = ifelse(understand_scheme == "01",
                                                                  "codes 0 + 1", "codes 1 + 2"),
            `Agreement with stored comprehension` = scales::percent(
              ifelse(understand_scheme == "01", agree_comp_01, agree_comp_12), 1)) %>%
  arrange(Collection) %>% kable()
```

### Sample

The NDAR sample is the kept WG administrations (one per child, item-profile check passed).
Wordbank WG norms stop at 18 months, so the main analyses use children aged 8–18 months.
Older children are scored against 18-month norms. Because gestures are near ceiling by
18 months in Wordbank, this is conservative for them: an older child must fall below
typical 18-month-olds.

```{r sample}
sample_tab <- nd_z %>% group_by(Collection = collection_id) %>%
  summarise(Children = n(), `Aged 8–18` = sum(in_norm_age), `Median age` = median(age),
            `% male` = scales::percent(mean(sex == "M"), 1),
            male = mean(sex == "M"),
            `Gestures scored` = scales::percent(mean(!is.na(fcg) & !is.na(later)), 1),
            `Comprehension scored` = scales::percent(mean(comp_ok & !is.na(comp)), 1)) %>%
  left_join(priors %>% select(Collection = collection_id, design_guess, prior), by = "Collection") %>%
  mutate(`Sex-implied ASD share` = round(pi_from_sex(male), 2)) %>%
  select(Collection, Design = design_guess, `Prior` = prior, everything(), -male)
kable(sample_tab)
```

Collection 2355 has only 8 children and very low gesture scores on every section. It
could be a coding difference, so it is shown but carries no weight in the conclusions.

## 2. Norms

```{r norms-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
long_raw <- bind_rows(
  wb_z %>% mutate(src = "Wordbank"),
  nd_z %>% filter(in_norm_age) %>%
    mutate(src = ifelse(collection_id %in% c(19, 2024), paste("NDAR", collection_id), "NDAR other"))) %>%
  select(src, age_n, prod, comp, fcg, later) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(prod, comp, fcg, later)) %>%
  mutate(name = factor(SCORES[name], SCORES[c("prod", "comp", "fcg", "later")]))
ggplot(long_raw, aes(age_n, value, colour = src)) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "line", linewidth = 1) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "point") +
  facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Wordbank = "grey30", `NDAR 19` = "#c0392b",
                                 `NDAR 2024` = "#2471a3", `NDAR other` = "#d68910")) +
  labs(x = "Age (months)", y = "Median count", colour = NULL,
       title = "Median scores by month, ages 8–18")
```

```{r z-by-collection}
zt <- nd_z %>% group_by(Collection = as.character(collection_id)) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), across(all_of(unname(zs)), ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  bind_rows(wb_z %>% summarise(Collection = "Wordbank", n = n(),
                               across(all_of(unname(zs)), ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE))))
names(zt)[-(1:2)] <- SCORES[names(zs)]
kable(zt, digits = 2, caption = "Median z-score by collection (all ages; negative = expected direction for autism)")
```

## 3. NDAR vs Wordbank

As in `07`, a first check is how well each score separates NDAR children from Wordbank
children: AUC = P(NDAR child scores lower than a Wordbank child). This mixes autism with
site and cohort differences, so it is an upper bound, not evidence of an autism signal.

```{r vs-wordbank}
groups <- list(`19` = 19, `2024` = 2024, `2027` = 2027, `2368` = 2368, `2878` = 2878)
auc_vs_wb <- function(d, v) auc_low(c(d[[v]], wb_z[[v]]), c(rep(TRUE, nrow(d)), rep(FALSE, nrow(wb_z))))
vs_wb <- map_dfr(names(zs), function(s) {
  v <- zs[[s]]
  map_dfr(names(groups), function(g) {
    d <- nd_z %>% filter(collection_id %in% groups[[g]])
    tibble(score = SCORES[[s]], group = g,
           `ages 8–18` = auc_vs_wb(d %>% filter(in_norm_age), v), `all ages` = auc_vs_wb(d, v))
  })
})
vs_wb %>% pivot_longer(c(`ages 8–18`, `all ages`)) %>%
  mutate(col = paste0(group, " (", name, ")")) %>%
  filter(!(group %in% c("2027", "2368") & name == "ages 8–18")) %>%
  select(score, col, value) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = value) %>%
  rename(Score = score) %>% kable(digits = 2)
```

Collection 2368 is the clearest autism collection (82% male, sex-implied share ≈ 1), but
almost all its children are older than 18 months. That makes its column the most direct
check of an autism signal, though only against 18-month norms.

### Within NDAR, at the same ages

The 2368 column above compares 30-month-olds with 18-month norms. A cleaner contrast is
within NDAR: 2368 against the children aged 19 months or more in collections 19 and 2027,
who have a much lower expected ASD share. This is the comparison on which the `07` profile
score failed (AUC .43 for ASD-heavy vs other collections).

```{r within-ndar}
older <- nd_z %>% filter(age >= 19, collection_id %in% c(19, 2027, 2368))
older %>% group_by(Collection = collection_id) %>%
  summarise(Children = n(), `Median age` = median(age), `% male` = scales::percent(mean(sex == "M"), 1),
            `Words produced` = median(prod), `Words understood` = median(comp, na.rm = TRUE),
            FCG = median(fcg, na.rm = TRUE), `Later gestures` = median(later, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Children aged 19+ months (medians)")
within <- map_dfr(names(zs), function(s) {
  v <- zs[[s]]; x <- older %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[v]])); case <- x$collection_id == 2368
  b <- replicate(B, { i <- c(sample(which(case), replace = TRUE), sample(which(!case), replace = TRUE))
                      auc_low(x[[v]][i], case[i]) })
  tibble(Score = SCORES[[s]], `AUC, 2368 vs 19 + 2027` = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]",
         auc_low(x[[v]], case), quantile(b, .025), quantile(b, .975)))
})
kable(within)
fcg_fit <- lm(elogit(fcg, 12) ~ age + elogit(prod, 396) + elogit(comp, 396) + elogit(later, 45) +
                I(collection_id == 2368), older)
fcg_coef <- summary(fcg_fit)$coefficients["I(collection_id == 2368)TRUE", ]
```

Within NDAR, a regression of FCG (empirical logit) on age, production, comprehension and
later gestures gives 2368 a coefficient of `r sprintf("%.2f (SE %.2f, p = %.3f)", fcg_coef[1], fcg_coef[2], fcg_coef[4])`.
Because 2368's children say far fewer words than the older children in 19 and 2027, this
comparison extrapolates across vocabulary levels. The Wordbank residual score, which
compares them with 18-month-olds of similar vocabulary, is the better-matched version.

## 4. The sex test

There are no child-level labels, so sex is used as the validation signal, as in `07`.
If a collection's ASD share is π, with P(male | ASD) = .80 and P(male | not ASD) = .51,
then boys are more likely to be autistic than girls by k = P(ASD | boy) − P(ASD | girl).
For any score whose true ASD-vs-non-ASD AUC is A:

AUC(boys score lower than girls) = .5 + k (A − .5) + (the ordinary sex gap in typical children).

The ordinary sex gap (girls ahead) is estimated from Wordbank on the same age-normed
scores and subtracted. That leaves an **implied ASD AUC**, A = .5 + excess / k.
Intervals come from `r B` bootstrap resamples of children, within collection and within
Wordbank, recomputing π from the resampled sex ratio each time.

Collection 2024 (infant siblings, 49% male, π ≈ 0) gives k ≈ 0 and serves as a placebo:
its excess should be about zero. The test itself rests on collection 19 (61% male,
π ≈ .34, k ≈ .27) and, at all ages, collection 2027. Its power is low: with k ≈ .27 a
score with A = .75 adds only about .07 to the boys-vs-girls AUC.

```{r sex-test}
sex_auc <- function(score, sex) auc_low(score, sex == "M")   # boys lower than girls
sex_stats <- function(d, wb, v) {
  base <- sex_auc(wb[[v]], wb$sex)
  per <- d %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]), sex %in% c("M", "F")) %>% group_by(collection_id) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), auc = sex_auc(.data[[v]], sex),
              k = sex_k(pi_from_sex(mean(sex == "M"))), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(excess = auc - base)
  pooled_in <- per %>% filter(collection_id != 2024, !is.na(auc))
  tibble(base = base, per = list(per),
         A_pooled = .5 + sum(pooled_in$n * pooled_in$excess) / sum(pooled_in$n * pooled_in$k))
}
run_sex <- function(d_all) {
  map_dfr(names(zs), function(s) {
    v <- zs[[s]]
    est <- sex_stats(d_all, wb_z, v)
    boot <- replicate(B, {
      db <- d_all %>% group_by(collection_id) %>% slice_sample(prop = 1, replace = TRUE) %>% ungroup()
      wbb <- wb_z[sample(nrow(wb_z), replace = TRUE), ]
      r <- sex_stats(db, wbb, v)
      c(A = r$A_pooled, setNames(r$per[[1]]$excess, r$per[[1]]$collection_id))
    })
    per <- est$per[[1]]
    tibble(score = SCORES[[s]], wordbank_sex_auc = est$base,
           A = est$A_pooled, A_lo = quantile(boot["A", ], .025, na.rm = TRUE),
           A_hi = quantile(boot["A", ], .975, na.rm = TRUE),
           per = list(per %>% mutate(
             lo = map_dbl(as.character(collection_id), ~ quantile(boot[.x, ], .025, na.rm = TRUE)),
             hi = map_dbl(as.character(collection_id), ~ quantile(boot[.x, ], .975, na.rm = TRUE)))))
  })
}
use <- c(19, 2024, 2027)
sex_in  <- run_sex(nd_z %>% filter(in_norm_age, collection_id %in% c(19, 2024)))
sex_all <- run_sex(nd_z %>% filter(collection_id %in% use))
```

```{r sex-table}
fmt_ci <- function(x, lo, hi) sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", x, lo, hi)
sex_tab <- function(r) r %>% transmute(
  Score = score, `Wordbank boys-lower AUC` = round(wordbank_sex_auc, 2),
  `19: excess` = map_chr(per, ~ with(filter(.x, collection_id == 19), fmt_ci(excess, lo, hi))),
  `2024 (placebo): excess` = map_chr(per, ~ with(filter(.x, collection_id == 2024), fmt_ci(excess, lo, hi))),
  `Implied ASD AUC` = fmt_ci(A, A_lo, A_hi))
kable(sex_tab(sex_in), caption = "Ages 8–18 (collection 19, k ≈ .27; collection 2024 placebo)")
kable(sex_tab(sex_all) %>% mutate(`2027: excess` = map_chr(sex_all$per, ~ with(
  filter(.x, collection_id == 2027), fmt_ci(excess, lo, hi)))),
  caption = "All ages, scored against norms clamped at 8–18 months (adds collection 2027)")
```

```{r sex-plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
bind_rows(sex_in %>% mutate(run = "Ages 8–18"), sex_all %>% mutate(run = "All ages")) %>%
  mutate(score = factor(score, rev(SCORES))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(A, score)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = .5, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = A_lo, xmax = A_hi), height = 0) + geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ run) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Implied ASD-vs-non-ASD AUC (from the excess boys-vs-girls gap)", y = NULL)
```

## 5. Which first communicative gestures?

For each FCG item, a Wordbank logistic regression on age, production and comprehension
gives each NDAR child's expected probability of "sometimes" or "often". The table shows
observed minus expected, averaged over children. A negative value means fewer NDAR
children show the gesture than Wordbank children with the same age and vocabulary.

```{r fcg-items, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
fcg_labels <- c("Shows (extends arm)", "Gives", "Points", "Waves bye-bye", "Arms up to be picked up",
                "Shakes head no", "Nods yes", "Hush", "Requests (open-close hand)",
                "Blows kisses", "Smacks lips (yum)", "Shrugs (all gone)")
wbm <- norms$wb %>% select(data_id, age_n, el_prod, el_comp)
wbi <- wbl$fcg_items[as.character(wbm$data_id), ]
nd_items <- nd$fcg_items
ndm <- nd_z %>% select(row, collection_id, age_n, el_prod, el_comp, in_norm_age, sex)
item_res <- map_dfr(seq_along(fcg_labels), function(j) {
  fit <- glm(y ~ splines::ns(age_n, 3) + splines::ns(el_prod, 3) + splines::ns(el_comp, 3),
             binomial, data = wbm %>% mutate(y = wbi[, j]))
  ndm %>% mutate(y = nd_items[, j], p = predict(fit, ndm, type = "response")) %>%
    filter(!is.na(y), !is.na(p)) %>%
    mutate(item = fcg_labels[j])
})
item_tab <- item_res %>%
  mutate(group = case_when(collection_id == 2368 ~ "2368 (ASD, all ages)",
                           in_norm_age & collection_id %in% c(19, 2024) ~ paste0(collection_id, " (8–18)"),
                           collection_id == 2027 ~ "2027 (all ages)", TRUE ~ NA)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(group)) %>%
  group_by(item, group) %>% summarise(n = n(), diff = mean(y - p), se = sd(y - p) / sqrt(n),
                                      .groups = "drop")
item_tab %>% mutate(item = factor(item, rev(fcg_labels))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(diff, item, colour = group)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = diff - 1.96 * se, xmax = diff + 1.96 * se),
                  position = position_dodge(width = .6), size = .3) +
  labs(x = "Observed − expected P(sometimes/often), given age and vocabulary", y = NULL, colour = NULL)
```

```{r save}
saveRDS(list(nd_z = nd_z, vs_wb = vs_wb, sex_in = sex_in, sex_all = sex_all, item_tab = item_tab),
        "data/nda_private/wg_gestures_gap.Rds")
```

## Findings

1. **A WG comprehension coding error is fixed.** Collections 19 and 2027 use a different
   comprehension coding (section 1). The fix changes no production data and no earlier
   result.
2. **First communicative gestures carry an autism-consistent signal beyond delay, in the
   one collection where it can be seen.** Collection 2368 is 82% male, with a median age of
   30 months and a median of 8 words. Its children show fewer first communicative gestures
   than Wordbank children with the same vocabulary and later-gesture scores
   (AUC ≈ .78). The most reduced gestures are pointing, showing, waving, requesting and
   giving (each 20–36 points below expected). These are the gestures the autism literature
   singles out.
   In the infant cohorts with a low expected ASD share (19, 2024, 2878), the same score sits
   at about .5 or below (.52, .43, .28). Their item deficits are smaller and less
   consistent: collection 19 is 13 points below on pointing and 9 on showing. Collection
   2024 is 22 below on showing but above expected on pointing. This is the contrast
   on which the `07` vocabulary profile failed. Here it goes the right way.
3. **The comprehension–production gap looks like an NDAR-wide difference, not an autism
   signal.** Comprehension given production is low in most NDAR collections, including
   the infant-sibling cohorts (AUC .58–.76). It separates 2368 from age-matched NDAR
   children only weakly. Words understood behaves like words produced: a delay measure.
4. **The sex test has no power here.** The implied ASD AUCs have intervals spanning most
   of 0–1. The placebo collection 2024 shows a positive excess on several scores, so the
   Wordbank sex gap does not transfer exactly. The test neither supports nor rules out any
   score. It would need several collections with intermediate ASD shares.

**Caveats.**
- The signal rests on a single collection of 40 children, whose NDA description also
  includes a non-autism developmental-delay group.
- Those children are older than any Wordbank WG norm. The residual scores compare them
  with 18-month-olds of similar vocabulary, so the comparison is "minimally verbal
  autistic toddlers vs late-talking 18-month-olds", which is roughly the clinically
  relevant contrast.
- Collection 2355 (n = 8) has implausibly low gesture scores and is set aside.

**For an ultra-short form**, the candidates are now a handful of FCG items (point, show,
give, wave, request), read relative to a vocabulary-level score. That is "gestures less
than their words predict", rather than any set of vocabulary words. To check it
properly:
- per-child labels, or more collections with older children on WG;
- a WG norm set beyond 18 months (Wordbank's own WG data stop at 18 months);
- the same check on the infant-sibling cohorts' later outcomes, if their WS follow-ups can
  be linked by GUID.
